level.title: Intermediate: كان, dual, commands, opinions
goals: Tell stories with كان and time words
Command politely and negate every tense

lessons.title: كان: was and were
lessons.learn: كان = was/were! كان كبيرا (he was big), كانت جميلة (she was beautiful). Stories: كان يدرس = he WAS studying (كان + present = was doing!). Unlock the storytelling past!

grammar.title: كان + word / كان + present
grammar.explain: كان مدرسا (he was a teacher), كانت جميلة (she was beautiful). كان يدرس = he was studying. كنتُ (I was), كنتَ (you-m were), كنتِ (you-f were)!
mistakes: Saying أنا كان — I-was is كنتُ!
Saying كانت جميلةٌ with ة-damma — كان's خبر takes -اً/-ةً!

lessons.title: Dual: كتابان
lessons.learn: Arabic has a DUAL — a special TWO form! كتابان (two books), يومان (two days), مدرستان (two schools-f). Just add -ان! 1–2 come AFTER nouns: كتاب واحد, يومان اثنان!

grammar.title: Dual with -ان
grammar.explain: كتاب→كتابان, يوم→يومان, مدرسة→مدرستان. Verbs too: يدرسان (they-two study)! Dual is everywhere — two eyes (عينان), two hands (يدان)!
mistakes: Forgetting feminine ة→ت: مدرستان, not مدرسةان!

lessons.title: The dual in real life: pairs
lessons.learn: Arabic has a third number. Two of anything takes one ending: -ان when it is the subject, -ين when anything acts on it. Pronouns follow: هما for 'they two' and both verbs agree.

grammar.title: Dual endings
grammar.explain: جاء الطالبان (both students came). رأيتُ الطالبَين (I saw both students). The dual also eats the plural: أخوان, not ثلاثة أخوين when there are exactly two.

mistakes.why: The dual already means two; اثنان is redundant.
After a verb, the dual takes -ين.

dialogue.en: They are in the library, studying together.
And did you wait for them long?
I waited two hours and then left.

lessons.title: Imperative: ادرس!
lessons.learn: Give orders! ادرس! (study! -m), ادرسي! (study! -f), اجلس! (sit!), تعال! (come!), اذهب! (go!). Soften with من فضلك: اجلس من فضلك = Please sit. Command + please = polite power!

grammar.title: Imperative: ادرس/ادرسي
grammar.explain: To men: ادرس، اجلس، تعال. To women add -ي: ادرسي، اجلسي، تعالي. To groups: ادرسوا! Negate with لا: لا تذهب! = Don't go!
mistakes: Saying ادرس to a woman — women get ادرسي!
Saying ما تذهب for don't — commands negate with لا!

lessons.title: Negation: لا، ما، لم، لن
lessons.learn: Four NEVERS! لا + present (لا أدرس = I don't study), ما + past (ما درستُ = I didn't study), لم + bare present (لم أدرس = I didn't study), لن + present (لن أدرس = I won't study). Pick by TENSE!

grammar.title: لا/لم/لن/ما by tense
grammar.explain: لا أدرس (I don't study), لم أدرس / ما درستُ (I didn't study), لن أدرس (I won't study). لم eats endings: لم يدرسْ (he didn't study)!
mistakes: Saying لا درستُ — past needs ما or لم!
Saying لن درستُ — لن loves PRESENT verbs!

lessons.title: Requests that stay polite, prohibitions that are not rude
lessons.learn: The imperative alone can sound like an order. Arabic softens it with لو سمحت or من فضلك, and forbids with لا + the jussive — a form that says 'don't', not 'you must not'.

vocab.en: if you would be so kind

grammar.title: Softening the imperative
grammar.pattern: imperative + min faḍlik / law samaḥt · lā + jussive
grammar.explain: أرسل لي الملف، لو سمحت. To forbid, Arabic says لا ترسل (don't send) — lighter than a rule. لا تنسَ أنّ الموعد غداً: don't forget that the appointment is tomorrow.

examples.en: Give me the number, if you would.

examples.t: يمكن أن نلتقي بعد العمل، بكل سرور.
examples.r: yumkin an naltqī baʿda al-ʿamal, bi-kull surūr.
examples.en: We can meet after work, with pleasure.

mistakes.why: After لا the verb is jussive: no final damma.
شكراً thanks; it does not soften a request.

dialogue.t: أرسل لي التقرير اليوم، لو سمحت.
dialogue.r: arsil lī al-taqrīr al-yawm, law samaḥt.
dialogue.en: Send me the report today, if you would.

dialogue.t: بكل سرور. هل يمكن أن أرسله مساءً؟
dialogue.r: bi-kull surūr. hal yumkin an ursilah masāʾan?
dialogue.en: With pleasure. May I send it in the evening?

dialogue.t: نعم، لكن لا تنسَ الاجتماع صباحاً.
dialogue.r: naʿam, lākin lā tansa al-ijtimāʿ ṣabāḥan.
dialogue.en: Yes — but don't forget the morning meeting.

dialogue.t: لن أنسى، سأرسل الملف قبل الثامنة.
dialogue.r: lan ansā, sa-ursil al-milaff qabla al-thāmina.
dialogue.en: I won't forget; I'll send the file before eight.

lessons.title: Opinions and أفضل
lessons.learn: Argue in Arabic! أعتقد أن… (I think that…), أفضل (better), أسوأ (worse), أكبر (bigger). أفعل pattern = comparatives! الأفضل = THE best. معك حق! = You're right!

grammar.title: أعتقد أن + أفعل comparatives

lessons.title: I partly agree: degrees of agreement
lessons.learn: Disagreement in Arabic usually starts with the part that is right. أوافق على… لكنّ… or صحيح أنّ… إلا أنّ… lets you disagree without turning the room against you.

vocab.en: on my side; as for me

grammar.title: Agree first, then limit
grammar.pattern: uwāfiq ʿalā X, lākin… · ṣaḥīḥ anna…, illā anna…
grammar.explain: أوافق على الفكرة، لكنّ التنفيذ صعب. صحيح أنّ الوقت ضيّق، إلا أنّ النتيجة تستحق. من جهتي أرى الأمر مختلفاً.

examples.en: I partly agree with what you said.

examples.t: صحيح أنّ السعر مرتفع، إلا أنّ الجودة أفضل.
examples.r: ṣaḥīḥ anna al-siʿr murtafiʿ, illā anna al-jawda afḍal.
examples.en: True, the price is high, but the quality is better.

examples.t: من جهتي، المشكلة في التوقيت لا في الخطة.
examples.r: min jihatī, al-mushkila fī al-tawqīt lā fī al-khuṭṭa.
examples.en: As for me, the problem is the timing, not the plan.

mistakes.why: Bare أوافق + لا cancels itself; name the degree instead.

items.q: Say aloud: أعتقد أن المترو أفضل.
Say: I think this is better

culture.text: كان is not simply 'was'. It turns the sentence it opens into a scene: كان الجوّ حاراً sets the weather as a backdrop, and a following clause reports what happened against it. Arabic storytelling leans on this 'scene then event' order far more than English does, which is why a learner who translates clause-by-clause produces correct sentences that still do not sound like a story.

reading.text: كان الوقت متأخراً حين وصلنا إلى المحطة، وكانت السماء تمطر. لم نجد سيارة أجرة، فمشينا على القدمين حتى الفندق. قال أخي: «لو وصلنا مبكراً، لوجدنا غرفة أفضل». ضحكتُ وقلت: «المهم أنّنا وصلنا بسلام». في الصباح كانت المدينة هادئة، وقد فتحت المقاهي أبوابها.
reading.gloss: It was late when we reached the station, and the sky was raining. We did not find a taxi, so we walked on foot as far as the hotel. My brother said, 'If we had arrived early, we would have found a better room.' I laughed and said, 'What matters is that we arrived safely.' In the morning the city was quiet, and the cafés had opened their doors.

listening.gloss: A: Why were you late? B: I couldn't — the road was crowded. A: And did you call? B: I tried twice, but the network was weak. I sincerely apologise.
